literal.prompt: В первых нескольких сотнях километров плавучей части шельфа Амри теряется более половины поступающего льда. Какой процесс вызывает эту потерю?

literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP describes the Amery Ice Shelf and states that more than 50% of ice flowing into it is lost through basal melting within the first few hundred kilometres after flotation begins (L315). The alternatives name distinct processes: buttressing slows inland ice discharge (AAP L306); marine ice sheet instability is a feedback on retrograde beds (NASEM L383-L385); calving is iceberg loss from the shelf front (AAP L302,L306). Only basal melting is the process explicitly responsible for the Amery statistic.
literalGroups.locator: AAP L315; NASEM L383-L385; AAP L302,L306

literalGroups.literal: Это базальное таяние. На шельфе Амри таким образом теряется более половины поступающего льда; таяние истончает шельф снизу и может ослаблять его подпирающее действие.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP L315 directly states the Amery statistic and defines basal melting as melting beneath the shelf where it interacts with the ocean. AAP L306 describes the shelf buttressing effect, supporting the explanation that shape/thinning can affect associated glacier flow.

literalGroups.literal: Базальное таяние идёт снизу при контакте основания шельфа с океаном; часть талой воды дальше на север вновь замерзает у основания как морской лёд.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP defines basal melting as melting beneath the shelf where it interacts with ocean water (L315); it also says some meltwater refreezes to the base as marine ice farther north (L315).

literalGroups.literal: Шельфовый ледник тормозит сток наземного льда, передавая сопротивление от боковых берегов и мелей.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP says shelves buttress inland ice and slow its discharge (L306); NSIDC explains backstress/pinning context (L71-L80).

literalGroups.literal: Неустойчивость морского щита возможна там, где ложе ниже моря углубляется в сторону материка.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NASEM describes MISI on retrograde beds and the positive retreat/thinning feedback (L383-L385); NASA JPL explains the inland-deepening bed and ocean access when grounding lines retreat (L29-L30).

literalGroups.literal: Айсберги откалываются от переднего края шельфа; поскольку он уже плавает, такое откалывание мало влияет на уровень моря.
literalGroups.primaryGround: AAP says shelves calve icebergs from their front (L302) and, because already afloat, calving does not significantly affect sea level (L306).

correctNoteNewFact.fact: Some meltwater from basal melting refreezes to the underside farther north as marine ice.
correctNoteNewFact.whyAdditional: The prompt gives the Amery loss statistic and the answer names basal melting; this downstream refreezing fact is additional and useful for understanding the process.

absoluteDifficulty.audienceGround: The question requires recalling a niche, quantitative Antarctic glaciology case: the Amery shelf loses more than half of inflowing ice through a particular process in the first few hundred kilometres after flotation. The alternatives are plausible specialist mechanisms (buttressing, MISI, calving), and the prompt does not name basal melting or describe its underside/ocean mechanism. A broad adult audience is unlikely to know this site-specific relation without study; selecting among the technical mechanisms is hard but remains one factual classification, not a multi-step calculation. Frozen HARD retained.
absoluteDifficulty.judgment: Absolute adult HARD is an editorial audience judgment grounded in the specific Amery mechanism/statistic and technical competing processes; source evidence proves the relation, not the audience estimate.
